summary: This Part II moves the complete Galois-symbol layer of K₂ symbols and Brauer groups beyond its motivic suppliers. It compares the existing Galois symbol with explicit Kummer cups, primitive-root contractions, cyclic symbol algebras, arithmetic norm-residue symbols, all-place reciprocity, Tate localization maps and the finite étale Chern class, retaining the root, residue and product signs at every comparison.

nodes.title: Primitive-root trivializations
nodes.statement: For m≥1 a unit in F, ζ∈F primitive of order m and j∈Z, construct τ_{ζ,j}:ZMod m≃μ_m^{⊗j} as an equivariant ZMod m-linear equivalence. It takes 1 to the tensor basis in positive weights, uses the dual basis in negative weights, and is the identity in weight zero.
hypotheses: Twists and all tensor/dual coherence maps are imported from M.1; ζ belongs to F, not just its separable closure.
proofSteps: At weight one compose zmodEquivZPowers with zpowers_eq and the coefficient embedding into the separable closure. Triviality of the Galois action follows because ζ lies in F.
Take tensor powers for j>0 and duals for j<0, using M.1’s evaluation and tensor coherence maps. The inverse sends the named basis to 1. The case m=1 is the equivalence between zero modules.
acceptance: Every root gives id at j=0, also for m=1.
At m=5, replacing ζ by ζ² multiplies weight-one coordinates by 2 and weight-two coordinates by 4=−1.
At m=5 the same change multiplies the weight −1 basis by 3, the inverse of 2.
For m=2 the unique primitive root −1 gives the canonical CFT weight-one trivialization.
Over Q, μ₃ has nontrivial Galois action and is not a trivial Z/3-module; its tensor square has trivial action. Defining every twist with χ instead of χ^j fails.

nodes.statement: For a discretely valued field F whose residue field k has m invertible, use the base-package tame symbol with ∂ᴹ{u,π}=ū and the cohomological residue with ∂κ(π)=1. nodes.title: Cyclic symbol algebra
nodes.statement: For a,b∈Fˣ, m≥2 invertible in F and ζ∈F primitive of order m, construct the F-algebra A_ζ(a,b) with basis e_{i,j}=X^iY^j, 0≤i,j<m, and relations X^m=a, Y^m=b, YX=ζXY. Products use ζ^{jk} and the a,b carry factors when reducing e_{i,j}e_{k,l}. No degree-m field extension is required.
hypotheses: F any field with the specified root and invertible coefficient; the monomial carrier is finite-dimensional, not an assumed cyclic field crossed product.
proofSteps: Define the twisted multiplication on the finite free F-module with the displayed basis. The scalar is ζ^{jk}a^{⌊(i+k)/m⌋}b^{⌊(j+l)/m⌋}. The carry identities and ζ^m=1 prove associativity and the unit formula.
Define X=e_{1,0},Y=e_{0,1}. The monomial relations give the universal map into any F-algebra containing a pair satisfying the three relations; reduction to normal form proves uniqueness.
Root-preserving scalar extension sends basis elements to the identically indexed basis. Prove its inverse, identity and composition on basis vectors.
acceptance: For m=2,ζ=−1, the universal maps give the existing quaternion algebra (a,b).
For a=c^m the algebra still has dimension m²; the radical field F(c) has degree 1 and is not its defining carrier.
At m=4 and a=c² the algebra has dimension 16, not the dimension 4 of its eventual quadratic corner.
The multiplication yields YX=ζXY; using ζ^{il} in place of ζ^{jk} yields the opposite convention.

nodes.statement: A_ζ(a,b) is central simple of degree m. After any field extension L/F with α^m=a it has a specified L-algebra isomorphism with Mat_m(L), requiring no m-th root of b.

nodes.title: Proper-degree matrix corner
nodes.statement: Let α^m=a, d=[F(α):F] and s=m/d. Then d divides m, c=α^d lies in F, c^s=a, and A_ζ(a,b)≃Mat_s(A_{ζ^s}(c,b)). The d=1 corner is F, with the evident trivial degree-one convention. This is an algebra equivalence after the specified root choice, and hence equality of Brauer classes.
hypotheses: The symbol-algebra hypotheses and α in a separable closure. Root containment makes F(α)/F cyclic of degree d, with image the order-d subgroup of μ_m.
proofSteps: The étale subalgebra E=F[X]/(X^m−a) has s field factors of degree d; the polynomials X^d−cζ^{rd}, 0≤r<s, give these factors.
Conjugation by Y cycles their primitive idempotents transitively. Choose the factor X^d=c. Its corner is generated by X and Y^s, has degree d, satisfies X^d=c,(Y^s)^d=b and Y^sX=ζ^sXY^s.

Use the conjugate idempotents and invertible Y to construct matrix units. The corner basis and dimension identify it with the degree-d symbol algebra. The resulting matrix equivalence is compatible with its inclusion into the original algebra.
acceptance: For m=4,a=c²,c nonsquare, obtain Mat₂(A_{ζ²}(c,b)); dimensions are 16 and 4 respectively.
For d=1 obtain Mat_m(F).
For d=m, the corner theorem is the identity presentation.
A proof that assumes t^m−a irreducible cannot discharge the m=4,a=c² test.

nodes.title: Cyclic algebra and cup comparison
nodes.statement: Under QFI 7B’s specified algebraic/cohomological Brauer equivalence, [A_ζ(a,b)]=β_ζ{a,b}. This equality uses the ordered cup κ(a)∪κ(b) and YX=ζXY and holds for every a,b∈Fˣ, including proper radical degree.
hypotheses: F any field; m≥2 invertible; ζ primitive in F. At m=2 compare with the already implemented quaternion theorem.
proofSteps: In the full-degree case put L=F(α), α^m=a and σ(α)=ζα. QFI’s crossed-product convention sends the carry cocycle d(g,h)=b^{⌊(i(g)+i(h))/m⌋} to the algebra with YX=ζXY.

Choose β^m=b and write κ(a)(g)=ζ^{i(g)}, κ(b)(g)=ζ^{j(g)}. The 1-cochain f(g)=β^{i(g)} has δf=d(g,h)ζ^{j(g)i(h)}. Thus [d]=−[κ(b)∪κ(a)]=[κ(a)∪κ(b)] after contraction, using the pinned explicitCup11_eq_neg_flip.

For d<m use the proper-degree matrix corner and the same cocycle with i(g) in the order-d subgroup; scalar carry is b. This is also β_ζ{a,b}, because the α-cocycle is ζ^{s i_d(g)} and contraction gives (ζ^s)^{i_d(g)j(g)}. Do not assume an irreducible degree-m radical extension.
Use QFI’s generic crossed-product comparison. On local fields also identify this map with CFT’s cup-to-Brauer map. Verify agreement with the current quaternion comparison at m=2.
acceptance: For Q₇,m=3,ζ reducing to 2, the class of A_ζ(3,7) and β_ζ{3,7} each have invariant 1/3.
For m=4,a=c² the proof agrees with the quadratic matrix corner.
Equality holds on each ordered symbol under the specified Brauer comparison, not just by comparing group orders.

nodes.title: Norm-residue map on K₂
nodes.statement: For a nonarchimedean local field F, m≥1 invertible in F and μ_m⊆F, construct the unique homomorphism N_{F,m}:K₂ᶜˡ(F)→μ_m(F) taking {a,b} to the supplier’s H_m(a,b)=Art_F(a)(b^{1/m})/b^{1/m}. The Artin map sends a uniformizer to arithmetic Frobenius.
hypotheses: F is complete discretely valued with finite residue field. In characteristic zero, m may be divisible by the residue characteristic. No primitive root is required to define N.
proofSteps: Import ClassicalArithmeticCompletion §§1.14 and 1.25: the scalar symbol, root-choice independence, bilinearity, skew symmetry, Steinberg relation and perfect pairing on Fˣ/F^{×m}.
Apply the Matsumoto universal property and equivalence from K2SymbolsBrauer T.2. Uniqueness follows from symbol generation; m-th powers in either slot give the identity.
acceptance: For Q₃,m=2, N{3,−1}=−1: the quadratic extension by √−1 is unramified and its norms have even valuation.
For Q₂,m=2 the tame symbol of {−1,−1} is 1, but N is −1; N does not factor through the tame symbol.
For Q_p,p odd,m=2, N is the quadratic residue character of the base tame symbol. Inversion of the tame convention is invisible at exponent two.
For m=1 all values are 1.

nodes.title: Splitting at the full roots of unity
nodes.statement: If the complete group μ(F) of roots of unity equals μ_m(F), then normResidueK2 is split surjective. More precisely choose ζ primitive of order m and a∈Fˣ with H_m(ζ,a)=ζ. The map ζ^i↦i{ζ,a} is a section μ_m→K₂ᶜˡ(F).

Perfectness of the supplier’s finite norm-residue pairing gives a character of exact order m on the ζ class, hence some a whose value H_m(ζ,a) is primitive. Replace a by a suitable unit exponent to make the value exactly ζ.
Bilinearity gives m{ζ,a}={ζ^m,a}=0, so the displayed section is well defined. Its composite with N is id. This repairs the primitive-value step noted in E3 and uses no downstream Moore theorem.

nodes.title: Total conic-solvability symbol
nodes.statement: For any field F and r,s∈F, define conicSymbol F r s∈Zˣ to be 1 if ∃x,y∈F, rx²+sy²=1, and −1 otherwise. This is a total solvability sign. For unit inputs and char F≠2 it is 1 exactly when s=x²−ry² has a solution. Bilinearity is asserted only after the local-field or real restriction.
hypotheses: The total definition works in every characteristic. The norm-equation bridge uses r,s∈Fˣ and char F≠2. The local comparison uses the supplier’s local hypotheses.
proofSteps: Define the value by decidable classical existence on the existing field carrier; no conic scheme or new Hilbert-symbol carrier is needed.

If a conic solution has y≠0 divide by y² to obtain the norm equation. If y=0 then r is a square and the split norm form represents every s in characteristic not two. For the reverse implication divide by a nonzero norm-coordinate; handle its zero case by the split difference-of-squares form.
Over R, no solution is equivalent to r≤0 and s≤0; if either is positive choose its inverse square root and set the other variable to zero. This includes the zero cases.
acceptance: conicSymbol R 0 0=−1; the strict-negative criterion for unit Hilbert symbols cannot be applied here.
For nonzero real r,s, value −1 iff both are negative.
conicSymbol Q₂ (−1) (−1)=−1.
On units of a nonarchimedean local F with 2 invertible, conicSymbol equals QFI’s existing hilbertSymbol.
Over Q, the values at (3,−1),(7,−1),(21,−1) are all −1, so the function is not multiplicative. Descent modulo 3 or 7 proves nonsolvability.
The values at (1,s) and (r,1−r) are 1, witnessed by (1,0) and (1,1).

nodes.title: Arithmetic invariant comparison
nodes.statement: For every nonarchimedean local field F, m≥1 invertible in F, μ_m⊆F and primitive ζ∈F, H_m(a,b)=ζ^{−e_m(inv_F β_ζ{a,b})}, where e_m:(Q/Z)[m]≃Z/m is characterized by e_m([k/m])=k. Equivalently the positive coordinate computes H_m(b,a). The same equality holds as homomorphisms on K₂(F).
hypotheses: Artin uses arithmetic Frobenius. e_m and the normalized Brauer invariant are imported from CFT; multiplication by m in Q/Z is zero and is not e_m. Residue-characteristic divisors of m are permitted when char F=0.
proofSteps: Use CFT’s normalized degree-two coordinate and its cup-to-Brauer theorem. Milne III Proposition 3.6 evaluates a character against Artin; III.4 identifies the positive contracted cup coordinate with Art_F(b)(a^{1/m})/a^{1/m}.
Skew symmetry of the supplier’s arithmetic symbol changes this to the inverse of H_m(a,b). With the fixed order κ(a)∪κ(b), the exponent is therefore negative for all m.
Root change multiplies β by u^{−1} and replaces ζ by ζ^u, so the final expression is unchanged. Extend from symbols by Matsumoto generation.
acceptance: For Q₇,m=3,ζ reducing to 2, inv β{3,7}=1/3, H₃(3,7)=ζ^{−1} and H₃(7,3)=ζ.
The expression remains the same under ζ↦ζ^u, β↦u^{−1}β.
At m=1 both sides are 1; at m=2 the minus sign is invisible and the result is QFI’s existing cohomological Hilbert comparison.
Replacing e_m by multiplication by m in Q/Z would make every value trivial; equality of norm kernels alone also fails to determine the scalar.

nodes.title: Product-normalized étale Chern comparison
nodes.statement: Let θ₂:K₂ᶜˡ(F)→K₂(F) be the base package’s raw Hurewicz comparison, ε=−1 its retained product sign, and θ₂♮=θ₂∘(ε·). For every field F, m≥1 invertible in F and x∈K₂ᶜˡ(F), c_{2,2}(red_m(θ₂♮x))=−h_{F,m}(x mod m) in H²_et(F,μ_m^{⊗2}). For the raw θ₂ the scalar is −ε=+1. The equality is on the integral-reduction image only.
hypotheses: Finite étale Chern maps and finite-coefficient products are imported from the low-degree M.8 contract. θ₂♮ is the actual product-normalized map of K2SymbolsBrauer §8.3; changing the raw comparison changes ε, not this intrinsic formula.
proofSteps: For prime-power coefficients apply the M.8 version of Soulé’s multiplication formula to c_{1,1}(red a)=κ(a) and c_{1,1}(red b)=κ(b). At i=j=k=k′=1 the coefficient is −(i+j−1)!/((i−1)!(j−1)!)=−1.

The external product therefore has Chern class −κ(a)×κ(b), and pullback along the diagonal gives the same minus sign for the internal product. The base product-normalized comparison sends {a,b} to that internal K₁ product.

Use the Kummer-cup dictionary and Matsumoto symbol generation to get the equality on all integral K₂. For arbitrary m use coefficient-reduction compatibility and the Chinese remainder decomposition into prime powers. At m=1 both sides are zero.
The Bockstein exact sequence limits the conclusion to integral reduction. It gives no formula on a chosen lift of the additional K₁(F)[m] quotient.
acceptance: For Q₇,m=3,{3,7}, the contracted cup invariant is 1/3 and the product-normalized Chern invariant is −1/3.
In a Z/6 coefficient coordinate a cup value 1 gives Chern value 5; its reductions are 1 mod 2 and 2 mod 3. CRT recovers 5, not 1.
Both the external product and its internal pullback have coefficient −1.
Replacing θ₂ by its negative also negates ε, leaving θ₂♮ and the intrinsic comparison unchanged.
No equality on the whole finite-coefficient K₂ is inferred when K₁(F)[m] is nonzero.
Both coefficient targets vanish at m=1.

sourceIssues.locator: Author copy dated 29 August 2013, III Lemma 6.9.1, p.241; no version-of-record assertion
sourceIssues.printed: The lemma claims that a degree-n central simple algebra over a field containing μ_n splits as soon as it has a noncentral element u with u^n=1. The proof identifies F[u] with F[t]/(t^n−1) without proving its minimal polynomial has degree n.
sourceIssues.correction: Require that u have minimal polynomial t^n−1, or equivalently that the n spectral idempotents all be nonzero. For the split symbol algebra this follows from its monomial basis; alternatively use the explicit splitting representation in KBII.2.
sourceIssues.reason: Take F=Q₅, which contains a primitive fourth root by Hensel lifting a root modulo 5. The quaternion D=(2,5) is division: its odd-residue Hilbert sign is −1 since 2 is nonsquare modulo 5. Then A=Mat₂(D) has degree 4 and is nonsplit. Its noncentral u=diag(1,−1) satisfies u⁴=1 but has minimal polynomial t²−1. This contradicts the author-copy statement. The corrected condition supplies n orthogonal nonzero idempotents, forcing the matrix size to be n.
